Use case: stylized-concept. One Freelancer li_pir_elite concept sheet with a substantial FORWARD-SWEPT Anubis-style tail and sculpted solid pedestal, following the variant condition below.
REFERENCE PRIORITIES:
Image 1 is the EXACT WING GEOMETRY AND ROOT reference. Each side has THREE separate triangular plates: amber rear plate, green MIDDLE plate, blue front plate. Reproduce ALL THREE shapes and three distinct stepped tips, recolored native pirate red, with only the source rear plate carrying a weapon pad. The green middle plate must NOT disappear into a seam. These are three overlapping whole blades, not three stripes on two blades. Their common root is on the LOWER FRONT EDGE OF THE MAIN BODY, AFTER the short neck behind the ribbed collar, not attached to the collar.
Image 2 locks the original cabin and collar: identical capsule, glazing divisions, width, length, three separated angular collar ribs. Do not redesign them.
Image 3 supplies ONLY the broad main hull and the two lateral rear engine pods. Do NOT copy its two-leaf wings or thin tail.
Image 4 supplies the Anubis/Order tail's deep interesting solid foundation and stepped structural volume, reversed fore-aft. No other Order parts.
Image 5 supplies native pirate Liberty materials and wing shape.

Make the NEW TAIL plus PEDESTAL a connected solid stern assembly behind the closed flush cargo hatch. Broad base, thick meaningful side faces, integrated lower wedge, two closely overlapping upper sections with modest possible nesting. It must have a substantial blunt form, not a thin pointed hook or spire. In side view nose LEFT: the upper tip and upper mass lie LEFT of their lower root. BOTH upper edges rise UP AND LEFT toward the cockpit. Keep the broad base aft and the forward overhang short and filled underneath. No car spoiler/bar connecting engines, no thin stalk, hollow framework, pipes, skulls or extra engines. Equipment pads belong to tail/base sides, never engine tops. Roof remains filled and flat.
Original cabin and ribbed collar remain the strongest Liberty cues. Restrained native Empire/Art Deco relief on the hull, mild functional wear. Original ordinary three-leaf fan wings retained, not redesigned. No added brow, heavy damage or excessive micro-detail.
Grey studio concept sheet with two LARGE views: FRONT-SIDE 3/4 and REAR 3/4. Cockpit LEFT in both, exhausts near right in rear view. Below SIDE FLIGHT nose LEFT, TOP, straight REAR, SIDE STOWED nose LEFT. At least three separated outer wing tips per side visible in top and large view. Show three full plates nested back along the flank in stowed view, not two. Every view is the same ship; forward tail rake identical. Tiny TOP/REAR must remain bilaterally symmetric, do not lean the tail sideways. Labels only ID and view names.
DISTINCT VARIANT CONDITION:
L73. FACETED SADDLE condition. The fixed pedestal is a wide six-sided planform: widest at its middle, clipped front/rear corners, tapered side walls and a deliberate low outer rim. This is one closed mechanical housing centered aft, not a ring or hollow frame. A narrow but thick two-section forward-swept tail grows from its longitudinal center. Lower tail side faces merge into the saddle's sloped planes. Use an angled equipment flat on each clipped side. Compared with the other variants, the silhouette change should be most obvious in TOP and REAR through the pedestal's faceted transverse spread. Label L73.
